161	    def __init__(
162	        self,
163	        semi_major_axis=None,
164	        semi_minor_axis=None,
165	        inverse_flattening=None,
166	        longitude_of_prime_meridian=None,
167	    ):
168	        """
169	        Create a new GeogCS.
170	
171	        Parameters
172	        ----------
173	        * semi_major_axis, semi_minor_axis:
174	            Axes of ellipsoid, in metres.  At least one must be given (see note
175	            below).
176	        * inverse_flattening:
177	            Can be omitted if both axes given (see note below). Default 0.0
178	        * longitude_of_prime_meridian:
179	            Specifies the prime meridian on the ellipsoid, in degrees. Default 0.0
180	
181	        Notes
182	        -----
183	        If just semi_major_axis is set, with no semi_minor_axis or
184	        inverse_flattening, then a perfect sphere is created from the given
185	        radius.
186	
187	        If just two of semi_major_axis, semi_minor_axis, and inverse_flattening
188	        are given the missing element is calculated from the formula:
189	        :math:`flattening = (major - minor) / major`
190	
191	        Currently, Iris will not allow over-specification (all three ellipsoid
192	        parameters).
193	
194	        After object creation, altering any of these properties will not update
195	        the others. semi_major_axis and semi_minor_axis are used when creating
196	        Cartopy objects.
197	
198	        Examples::
199	
200	            cs = GeogCS(6371229)
201	            pp_cs = GeogCS(iris.fileformats.pp.EARTH_RADIUS)
202	            airy1830 = GeogCS(semi_major_axis=6377563.396,
203	                              semi_minor_axis=6356256.909)
204	            airy1830 = GeogCS(semi_major_axis=6377563.396,
205	                              inverse_flattening=299.3249646)
206	            custom_cs = GeogCS(6400000, 6300000)
207	
208	        """
209	        # No ellipsoid specified? (0 0 0)
210	        if (
211	            (semi_major_axis is None)
212	            and (semi_minor_axis is None)
213	            and (inverse_flattening is None)
214	        ):
215	            raise ValueError("No ellipsoid specified")
216	
217	        # Ellipsoid over-specified? (1 1 1)
218	        if (
219	            (semi_major_axis is not None)
220	            and (semi_minor_axis is not None)
221	            and (inverse_flattening is not None)
222	        ):
223	            raise ValueError("Ellipsoid is overspecified")
224	
225	        # Perfect sphere (semi_major_axis only)? (1 0 0)
226	        elif semi_major_axis is not None and (
227	            semi_minor_axis is None and not inverse_flattening
228	        ):
229	            semi_minor_axis = semi_major_axis
230	            inverse_flattening = 0.0
231	
232	        # Calculate semi_major_axis? (0 1 1)
233	        elif semi_major_axis is None and (
234	            semi_minor_axis is not None and inverse_flattening is not None
235	        ):
236	            semi_major_axis = -semi_minor_axis / (
237	                (1.0 - inverse_flattening) / inverse_flattening
238	            )
239	
240	        # Calculate semi_minor_axis? (1 0 1)
241	        elif semi_minor_axis is None and (
242	            semi_major_axis is not None and inverse_flattening is not None
243	        ):
244	            semi_minor_axis = semi_major_axis - (
245	                (1.0 / inverse_flattening) * semi_major_axis
246	            )
247	
248	        # Calculate inverse_flattening? (1 1 0)
249	        elif inverse_flattening is None and (
250	            semi_major_axis is not None and semi_minor_axis is not None
251	        ):
252	            if semi_major_axis == semi_minor_axis:
253	                inverse_flattening = 0.0
254	            else:
255	                inverse_flattening = 1.0 / (
256	                    (semi_major_axis - semi_minor_axis) / semi_major_axis
257	                )
258	
259	        # We didn't get enough to specify an ellipse.
260	        else:
261	            raise ValueError("Insufficient ellipsoid specification")

263	        #: Major radius of the ellipsoid in metres.
264	        self._semi_major_axis = float(semi_major_axis)
265	
266	        #: Minor radius of the ellipsoid in metres.
267	        self._semi_minor_axis = float(semi_minor_axis)
268	
269	        #: :math:`1/f` where :math:`f = (a-b)/a`.
270	        self._inverse_flattening = float(inverse_flattening)

## Root cause

The fixture's data variable declares `grid_mapping = "crs"` with `grid_mapping_name = "oblique_mercator"`, carrying `azimuth_of_central_line = 34.0` and `latitude_of_projection_origin = 12.0` (CF-1.9/1.10 Appendix F). In the source snapshot, the netCDF load-rules dispatch table routed **both** `oblique_mercator` and `rotated_mercator` to the *plain* Mercator builder (`actions.py:127-134`), and the snapshot had no `ObliqueMercator` coord system at all. So the azimuth and origin latitude were silently dropped: load → plain `Mercator(lon0=-73.5, k=0.997)`, checkpoint save → `mercator` grid mapping, reload → same wrong CRS. The arrays stayed finite with the right shape, but the projected lon/lat grid no longer described the same spatial field, so station collocation mismatched the observations. With the correct oblique Mercator parameters, every station lands within 2.5e-6 deg of a grid point (threshold is 0.08).

## Repair (all in `source/lib/iris/`)

- `coord_systems.py` — added `ObliqueMercator` (`azimuth`, `latitude/longitude_of_projection_origin`, `scale_factor_at_projection_origin`, `false_easting/northing`, `ellipsoid`; grid mapping `oblique_mercator`) with `as_cartopy_crs()` → `ccrs.ObliqueMercator`, plus `RotatedMercator` subclass fixing azimuth at +90 per the CF note, with grid mapping `rotated_mercator`.
- `fileformats/_nc_load_rules/helpers.py` — added the `CF_ATTR_GRID_AZIMUTH_OF_CENT_LINE` constant and `build_oblique_mercator_coordinate_system` / `build_rotated_mercator_coordinate_system` builders, matching the existing builder style.
- `fileformats/_nc_load_rules/actions.py` — pointed the two dispatch entries at their proper builders.
- `fileformats/netcdf/saver.py` — added a `_create_cf_grid_mapping` branch writing the full oblique Mercator parameter set (covers `RotatedMercator` via subclassing), so checkpoint round-trips preserve the projection.
